pathway.title: Group 1 Automotive Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage after the Hennessy purchase is the credit's main pressure point, and the latest balance sheet understates it. Net leverage was 2.82x at the end of 2024 and 4.29x at the end of 2025; it eased to 3.30x at 30 September 2026 because a large 2025 impairment left the trailing window and disposals raised USD 481.8 million, and it is about 4.73x pro forma for the payment of about USD 1.3 billion on 2026-10-19, before any earnings, cash or liabilities acquired. The company's own covenant ratios, 3.26x leverage against a ceiling of 5.75x, are measured before the purchase on definitions that were not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

- Aftersales and finance and insurance anchor earnings, but the anchor is slipping at the edges. Those two lines were 70.55% of gross profit in the first nine months of 2026, yet total gross profit fell 5.61% (7.06% in the third quarter) and selling, general and administrative expenses took 71.04% of gross profit against 69.82% a year earlier. The United States earns 90.93% of group pre-tax income and its income fell 18.67% in nine months and 22.80% in the quarter, so the return of the United Kingdom to a USD 39.6 million profit from a USD 100.3 million loss, which followed 2025 impairments, is the only offset. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

- Cash conversion is thin against the enlarged debt. Free cash flow was USD 226.3 million in the last twelve months, 24.86% of EBITDA against 49.64% in 2025 (22.62% against 39.44% before impairments and restructuring, so the fall is real but smaller than the unadjusted figures suggest), because operating cash flow fell to 46.24% of EBITDA in nine months from 82.61% as payables and accruals absorbed USD 145.3 million. The new notes add about USD 80 million of annual interest, so at the last-twelve-months pace of free cash flow the purchase price would take 5.74 years to repay before dividends; the three disposals completed after quarter-end, for about USD 235 million, are the nearer source of deleveraging. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67

- Liquidity before the purchase is large, and after it is not established. Company-defined liquidity was USD 2,477.0 million at 30 September 2026 against USD 883.0 million at the end of 2025, but the price equals 52.48% of it, cash of USD 881.5 million is USD 418.5 million short of the price, and Acquisition Line availability of USD 1,442.4 million is USD 295.3 million below commitment less letters of credit, a gap the filings attribute to covenant calculations they do not print. The balance of the price came from sources the filings do not allocate, so cash and liquidity after the payment are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60

- Refinancing risk is back-ended but not remote. The 2028 notes of USD 750.0 million fall due in about 21 months, and the USD 1,250.0 million placed at par in September 2026 shows access to the market, but the quarter-end fair values were below par for all four note series, at 96.93% and 95.62% of principal for the 2032 and 2035 notes eight days after issue; refinancing the 2028 notes at the 2032 coupon would add about USD 16.9 million of annual interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C23; calculation C24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Shareholder payouts are the discretionary lever and have been cut. Repurchases and dividends were 136.73% of free cash flow in 2025 but 52.66% in the first nine months of 2026, with repurchases of USD 72.4 million all in the first quarter; USD 306.3 million of authorization remains with no expiry, so a resumption would divert cash from debt reduction when leverage is highest. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-03-31_gpi-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68

- Asset protection is mostly intangible and layered. Goodwill and franchise rights equal 94.78% of equity, leaving tangible equity of USD 160.1 million; secured real estate debt of USD 1,112.2 million ranks ahead of the unsecured notes, which are guaranteed only by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries; and floorplan notes payable of USD 2,123.9 million sit outside the debt figure and fund 82.53% of inventory. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C22; calculation C26; calculation C28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23

runs.text: The main strengths are four. The aftersales and finance and insurance profit pool supplied 70.55% of nine-month 2026 gross profit, and U.S. same-store parts and service gross profit was flat while the vehicle lines fell, which steadies debt service through the vehicle cycle. Liquidity before the purchase, at USD 2,477.0 million on the company's definition, and reported covenant ratios of 3.26x against a 5.75x ceiling and 2.78x against a 1.20x floor, give room that the weaker earnings have not yet used. Owned property, at 71.26% of dealerships, and disposal proceeds of USD 481.8 million in nine months give secured borrowing and asset-sale options. Fixed-rate unsecured funding, with USD 1,250.0 million placed in 2026 and no note or revolver maturity before the 2028 notes of USD 750.0 million, gives time. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C19; calculation C27; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

The main weaknesses are five. Net leverage is about 4.73x pro forma and only 24.86% of EBITDA reached free cash flow in the last twelve months, so deleveraging is slow. Gross profit is falling faster than costs, with selling, general and administrative expenses at 71.04% of gross profit. Earnings are concentrated, with the United States earning 90.93% of group pre-tax income while its income fell 18.67%. Goodwill and franchise rights equal 94.78% of equity, so the cushion beneath the debt is mostly intangible and would grow with the Hennessy goodwill. Manufacturers control vehicle supply, franchise rights and USD 64.9 million of floorplan assistance, and liquidity after the purchase is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C13; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

cells.text: Franchised automotive retailer: sells and leases new and used cars and light trucks, arranges vehicle financing, sells service and insurance contracts, repairs and maintains vehicles and sells parts at retail and wholesale; 32 collision centers at 2025-12-31

Calls itself a leading operator in automotive retail, with a strategy of local market focus, operational excellence, a differentiated parts and service business and disciplined capital allocation; describes aftersales as a resilient, counter-cyclical complement to vehicle retailing
Delaware corporation with headquarters in Houston, Texas (leased); common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange under GPI; operations in 17 U.S. states and 60 U.K. towns and cities
Automotive retail through franchised dealerships; two reportable segments, the U.S. and the U.K., with income before income taxes as the measure used to allocate resources

145 U.S. and 104 U.K. dealerships at 2026-09-30, against 145 and 109 at 2025-12-31 and 145 and 114 at 2024-12-31; the Hennessy acquisition adds 10 dealerships and one collision center in Greater Atlanta from 2026-10-19

First nine months of 2026 revenues: new vehicles 48.39%, used retail 32.02%, used wholesale 2.62%, parts and service 12.96%, finance and insurance 4.01%; gross profit: parts and service 45.54% and finance and insurance 25.01%, together 70.55%

U.S. 72.20% and U.K. 27.80% of revenues in the first nine months of 2026; of 2025 new vehicle unit sales, the U.S. was 72.4% and the U.K. 27.6%, with Texas alone 31.6%

Relies on manufacturers for all new vehicle inventory; franchise agreements are non-exclusive, most U.S. agreements run indefinitely, many U.K. agreements have two-year rolling terms and may be ended for network consolidation or unapproved ownership changes; Toyota and Lexus are the largest share of unit sales, the percentage is not stated in the text
Retail consumers; no customer concentration is disclosed; manufacturers reimburse warranty work and hold the franchise relationship

Public company; no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed; 32 holders of record at 2026-02-06; 11,947,272 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 with 52.04% of issued shares held in treasury; Conifer Management, L.L.C. and affiliates are one of the largest stockholders, capped at 19% by agreement

Nine directors signed the 2025 annual report, including a chairman separate from the chief executive officer, who is also a director; the 2026-10-29 report refers to a board of 10 expanding to 11; four named board committees; Deloitte & Touche LLP is the auditor
20,452 employees at 2025-12-31, of whom 13,563 in the U.S. and 6,889 in the U.K.; 20,413 a year earlier
181 of 254 dealerships stand on owned real estate at 2025-12-31 (71.26%); 179 of 259 a year earlier

2024: Inchcape Retail (54 locations, approximately USD 517.0 million), nine other U.S. dealerships (USD 690.4 million) and five other U.K. dealerships (USD 110.1 million); 2025: four U.S. (USD 531.7 million) and four U.K. (USD 16.4 million) dealerships; first nine months of 2026: four U.S. (USD 219.0 million) and three U.K. (USD 0.6 million); then Hennessy at approximately USD 1.3 billion
The debt securities are described as rated just below investment grade; the agency, rating and outlook are not stated

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-07-30 Group 1 agreed to buy the assets of 10 automobile dealerships and one collision center in Greater Atlanta, Georgia, with related real estate and leaseholds, and completed the purchase on 2026-10-19 for approximately USD 1.3 billion, subject to post-closing adjustments. USD 80.0 million of the price sits in an indemnity escrow, with 25% released three months after closing, a further 25% after nine months and the remainder after 18 months, subject to pending claims. The purchase is accounted for as a business combination, but the allocation of the price, the goodwill and the pro forma information were incomplete when the report was issued, and manufacturers may impose conditions on the transfer of the 12 franchises. Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67

The purchase was financed with the net proceeds of two private placements on 2026-09-22, each of USD 625.0 million issued at par: notes due February 2032 and notes due February 2035, together with cash on hand. The notes are unsecured, guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries, subordinated to senior secured debt and to the liabilities of non-guarantor subsidiaries, and may have to be repurchased on certain asset sales or a change of control; issuance costs were USD 15.9 million and the company expects about USD 80 million of added annual interest expense. A 364-day senior unsecured bridge commitment of up to USD 1.25 billion from JPMorgan, obtained on 2026-07-30, was terminated unused at closing, and the part of the price paid from cash on hand is not stated. Basis: calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67

In September 2026 the company also signed a master credit agreement with Bank of America for mortgage term loans of up to USD 190.3 million at Term SOFR plus 145 basis points, maturing on 2033-09-23, fully drawn at 2026-09-30 and secured by mortgages on the financed properties, with Group 1 Realty, Inc. as borrower. On 2026-09-21 it signed the stockholder agreement with Conifer, which caps that holder at 19% and, from 2026-11-01, expands the board from 10 to 11 directors. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70

Other 2026 activity was smaller: four U.S. dealerships and three U.K. dealerships were bought in the first nine months for USD 219.0 million and USD 0.6 million, one Honda and one Toyota dealership were sold in the third quarter for USD 90.8 million, and seven U.S. dealerships with USD 396.9 million of assets are held for sale, three of them already sold for about USD 235 million after quarter-end. Disposals in the nine months produced a net pre-tax gain of USD 44.2 million in the U.S. and a loss of USD 8.1 million in the U.K.; the date of the three later sales and the use of the proceeds are not stated. Basis: calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14

Earlier transactions set the base: Inchcape Retail was acquired on 2024-08-01 with 54 dealership locations and three collision centers in the U.K. for approximately USD 517.0 million, USD 500.0 million of notes due January 2030 were issued on 2024-07-30, and the revolving credit facility was extended to 2030-05-30 and enlarged from USD 2.5 billion to USD 3.5 billion on 2025-05-30. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_gpi-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127

fields.value: Source readiness for Group 1 Automotive Inc, a listed automotive retailer with dealerships in the United States and the United Kingdom, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five filings supplied: annual reports for the years ended 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31 and quarterly reports for the quarters ended 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30. No credit rating, bond quote, peer set, legal agreement or portfolio input was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the signature dates printed in each report; the filing dates are not stated. No handoff from another module was supplied to this module, so none is listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five Group 1 Automotive filings support a filing-based credit snapshot at 30 September 2026, but not ratings, legal-document, market-pricing or post-acquisition work, so creditors should treat every balance-sheet figure as before the USD 1.3 billion Hennessy purchase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings print no credit rating beyond a statement that the debt is rated just below investment grade, no executed debt agreements, no dated bond quotes beyond quarter-end fair values of the notes and no peer financials, and the company reports no EBITDA, so those items are not established and leverage has to be derived from statement lines or taken from the company's own covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third-quarter cash flow statement covers nine months only, so a standalone quarter needs the six-month statement subtracted, and the latest source was signed 20 days before the as-of date with nothing later supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One gap is material and four are minor. No conflict between the five filings was found; the printed totals tie to their parts within rounding of USD 0.1 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Group 1 Automotive Inc, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, coverage and post-balance-sheet events from the five filings supplied and the Source readiness analysis, with the latest balance sheet at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the signature dates printed in each report; the filing dates are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 3,004.7 million, 3.30x last-twelve-months EBITDA, at 30 September 2026, but the USD 1.3 billion Hennessy payment after quarter-end lifts it to about 4.73x before acquired earnings, so creditors should underwrite the higher figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That EBITDA is unadjusted and carries USD 78.7 million of non-cash asset impairments in the last twelve months; adding them and restructuring charges back gives 3.00x, and the company reports its own covenant ratios, 3.26x leverage against a ceiling of 5.75x and 2.78x fixed charge coverage against a floor of 1.20x, as within their limits. Cash interest was covered 3.30x, and the new notes add about USD 80 million of annual interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Net leverage rose from 2.82x at the end of 2024 to 4.29x at the end of 2025 because net debt grew by USD 788.2 million while EBITDA fell by USD 167.1 million to USD 855.1 million, with asset impairments of USD 192.8 million and selling, general and administrative expenses up from USD 2,179.2 million to USD 2,545.5 million; in the same year acquisitions and share repurchases absorbed USD 1,101.6 million of cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C28; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–95

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The easing to 3.30x at 30 September 2026 came from the USD 123.9 million third-quarter 2025 impairment leaving the twelve-month window and from USD 481.8 million of disposal proceeds in 2026, not from lower borrowing: net debt fell by USD 193.8 million in the quarter, but total debt rose to USD 3,886.2 million, 4.27x EBITDA, because the new notes pre-funded the Hennessy payment; the cash of USD 881.5 million nets against that debt only until the payment is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid was USD 276.2 million in the last twelve months against USD 223.6 million in 2024, so EBITDA cover fell from 4.57x to 3.30x, and the company expects the two new note series to add about USD 80 million of annual interest expense, before any earnings from Hennessy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2024-12-31_gpi-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 129

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was USD 174.9 million against USD 373.1 million a year earlier as operating cash flow fell by USD 223.3 million, with payables and accruals absorbing USD 145.3 million against USD 24.5 million; share repurchases fell to USD 72.4 million from USD 249.8 million, so shareholder returns are not the pressure on cash this year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C32; calculation C31; calculation C34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The U.K. segment moved from a loss before income taxes of USD 100.3 million, which included USD 126.5 million of impairments, in the first nine months of 2025 to a profit of USD 39.6 million in 2026, while the U.S. segment's income fell from USD 487.9 million to USD 396.8 million and group revenue was USD 802.7 million lower, so the group recovery rests on a U.K. rebound while U.S. earnings weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower leverage reading is that unadjusted EBITDA is after non-cash impairments, so net leverage is 3.00x on the excluding basis, and the company reports covenant leverage of 3.26x against a 5.75x ceiling, which its definitions, not supplied here, make hard to compare; disposals could also cut debt, since three dealership sales brought about USD 235 million and would alone take net leverage to 3.04x. The view would change with Hennessy's earnings and purchase accounting, which the quarterly report does not give: enough acquired EBITDA would pull the 4.73x pro forma figure down, while a weaker U.S. segment would push it up.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C18; calculation C36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

fields.value: EBITDA is calculated by this module and unadjusted, so it carries asset impairments and restructuring charges.

fields.value: The stack leaves out the 4.00% senior notes, finance leases, other debt and the revolving credit facility because no source states their rank.

fields.value: No bridge can be stated because the issuer states no adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The position after the Hennessy closing is not established: the latest balance sheet is at 30 September 2026, the acquisition closed on 19 October 2026 for approximately USD 1.3 billion, and the report says purchase accounting and pro forma information were incomplete; the pro forma net debt in this analysis applies the rounded consideration to quarter-end net debt and includes no acquired earnings, cash or liabilities. Severity: High. Action: obtain the closing report and the next quarterly or annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - There is no debt maturity ladder at 30 September 2026: the ladder at 31 December 2025 includes an Acquisition Line balance of USD 964.0 million that was repaid in 2026 and omits the 2032 and 2035 notes, amortization of mortgage loans and finance leases is not printed, and only current maturities of USD 261.8 million are stated. Severity: Medium. Action: build the wall from the instrument table and treat unscheduled amortization as not established, or obtain an updated maturity table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt stack is incomplete because no source states rank or security for the 4.00% senior notes of USD 750.0 million, finance leases of USD 285.2 million, other debt of USD 16.4 million or the revolving credit facility, so they are left out of the stack and of any senior or secured subtotal. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the indentures and the revolving credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is calculated, not reported: the issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, floorplan interest is presented below income from operations, and unadjusted EBITDA is after asset impairments and restructuring charges; the headline ratios are before floorplan interest and unadjusted, with the other views shown as Analyst Judgement. Severity: Medium. Action: none available from the filings; the company's own covenant ratios are shown beside the derived ones.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is printed only as a cumulative figure that includes floorplan interest and swap settlements, with no discrete quarter and no split between floorplan and other debt, so cover on EBITDA after floorplan interest is not calculable and a standalone third quarter is nine months less six months. Severity: Medium. Action: none available from the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interim balance sheets for 2025 are not printed in the 2026 quarterly reports, so net debt at 31 March, 30 June and 30 September 2025 is not established and the leverage trend uses the two year-ends and the three 2026 quarter-ends. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly reports if a full quarterly series is needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings round each line, so the printed activity totals and exchange effect differ from the printed net change in cash by USD 0.1 million in Q1 2026, H1 2025 and H1 2026, where Net Cash Change is not supplied, and the 2026-09-30 debt, liquidity and other-debt totals differ from their parts by USD 0.1 million. Severity: Low. Action: none; the differences are rounding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines printed as a dash are carried as not supplied, not as zero, and a line the report for a period does not print is not supplied for that period; this affects other operating (income) expense, other (income) expense, discontinued operations, restructuring charges, escrow payments for acquisitions, other investing, borrowings of senior notes and the lines for current liabilities held for sale; two cash flow lines printed only as dashes in every column shown, proceeds from sale of discontinued operations and other financing, are omitted. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Per-share and share-count lines and operating measures such as units sold and gross profit per unit are not carried in the statement tables or the KPI dashboard, which hold dollar amounts in millions. Severity: Low. Action: obtain them from the results discussion if unit economics are required.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Group 1 Automotive Inc, a listed automotive retailer, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, governance, operating model and transaction facts in the five filings supplied (annual reports for 2024 and 2025 and quarterly reports to 2026-09-30) and in the Source readiness analysis. No sponsor, credit rating, legal agreement, proxy statement or post-closing report was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the signature dates printed in each report; the filing dates are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Group 1 is a franchised car retailer with no disclosed controlling owner, so creditors depend on management's capital allocation and on manufacturer approvals, and the USD 1.3 billion Hennessy purchase, funded by new unsecured notes, is the largest test of that discretion. Parts, service and finance and insurance earned 70.55% of gross profit in the first nine months of 2026, which steadies earnings against the vehicle cycle, but 2025 shareholder payouts of USD 580.4 million exceeded net income of USD 325.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and ownership risk is medium. The Conifer stockholder agreement caps that holder at 19%, one percentage point under the 20% change-of-control level that the company cites for some manufacturer agreements, so the pace of buybacks is tied to franchise approvals, while ownership percentages, director independence and related-party dealings are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Aftersales and finance and insurance, not vehicle sales, carry the profit, so earnings are steadier than the revenue mix implies. New vehicles were 48.39% of revenues but 19.90% of gross profit in the first nine months of 2026, while parts and service and finance and insurance together were 70.55% of gross profit, against 69.58% in 2025 and 67.77% in 2024. The cushion is wearing at the edges: gross profit fell 5.6% as used retail units fell 8.7% and new retail units fell 4.8%, finance and insurance gross profit fell 8.0%, and selling, general and administrative expenses rose to 71.0% of gross profit from 69.8%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor or controlling shareholder is disclosed, which removes sponsor-extraction risk but also any sponsor backstop. The largest named holder, Conifer, has agreed to a 19% ceiling, a standstill through at least the 2029 annual meeting and to vote with the board during a support period, and it can designate one director while it holds at least 5%; its actual percentage is not disclosed, and when the support period ends the standstill lapses and its voting commitment narrows to holdings above 20%. More than half of issued shares, 52.04%, are already held in treasury, so each further buyback raises every remaining holder's percentage, Conifer's included.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder payouts, not operations, are the discretionary credit risk, and they fell sharply in 2026. In 2025 repurchases of USD 554.8 million and dividends of USD 25.6 million came to 178.47% of net income and 136.73% of free cash flow, in a year when acquisitions absorbed a further USD 546.8 million. In the first nine months of 2026 repurchases fell to USD 72.4 million from USD 249.8 million a year earlier, all in the first quarter; none followed in the second or third quarter and the filings give no reason. The dividend rate was raised 10% to USD 2.20 a share, and USD 306.3 million of authorization remains with no expiry.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_gpi-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Hennessy purchase raises acquisition, integration and concentration risk more than it adds diversification. At approximately USD 1.3 billion it is 2.51x the Inchcape consideration, it adds 10 dealerships representing 12 franchises in one metropolitan market, and purchase accounting was incomplete when the report was issued. It was funded by USD 1,250.0 million of unsecured senior notes issued at par on 2026-09-22 plus cash on hand, which add about USD 80 million of annual interest expense; a USD 1.25 billion bridge commitment was terminated unused, and a seller indemnity escrow of USD 80.0 million, released in three stages over 18 months, cushions post-closing claims. Disposals are recycling capital: seven U.S. dealerships are held for sale and three were sold after quarter-end for about USD 235 million, but the filings do not say how the proceeds were used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Manufacturer relationships are the main structural dependency and the channel through which an ownership event could hurt creditors. Franchise agreements are non-exclusive and may be ended or not renewed for network consolidation or unapproved ownership changes, and framework agreements with most major manufacturers restrict acquisitions and financing and contain change-of-control clauses tied to share ownership; U.S. state law requires good cause to end a franchise but the U.K. has no equivalent franchise statute. Toyota and Lexus are the largest share of unit sales but the size is not stated in the text, and Toyota has announced it will reduce dealership financial assistance, which matters because manufacturer floorplan assistance of USD 64.9 million covered almost all of USD 66.3 million of floorplan interest in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The U.K. is being repositioned while the U.S. carries the profit, so the earnings base is concentrating in the U.S. The U.K. lost USD 113.2 million before tax in 2025 after USD 128.2 million of impairments and USD 28.4 million of restructuring, and earned USD 39.6 million in the first nine months of 2026 against a loss of USD 100.3 million a year earlier, while the U.S. earned USD 396.8 million, down 18.67% from USD 487.9 million. Chinese brands grew from about 8% to about 13% of U.K. new vehicle sales between 2024 and 2025, which the group is answering with Geely and Chery locations, and the outcome of the U.K. motor-finance redress scheme is not reported after the annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 134–135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring of operations and debt but not of ownership or board independence. The accounts carry an audit opinion that they present fairly and an effective internal control conclusion, although one 2025 acquisition with USD 157.4 million of assets and USD 94.4 million of revenues was excluded from the control assessment; the chairman is separate from the chief executive, and four board committees are named. The annual report's signature page lists nine directors while the latest quarterly report refers to a board of 10; directors, pay, related-party dealings and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and two executive separation agreements were signed in 2025 without roles stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C19; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 87–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk judgement is behavioural: nothing in the filings shows value moving to a controlling holder, repurchases stopped after the first quarter of 2026, the dividend rose only 10%, Hennessy was funded with fixed-rate notes and cash with the bridge left undrawn, disposals brought USD 481.8 million of proceeds in nine months, and the largest named holder accepted a standstill. Against a comfortable view, payouts exceeded earnings in 2025, the purchase concentrates integration risk in one market before any acquired earnings are reported, and goodwill and franchise rights equal 94.78% of equity before Hennessy's goodwill is added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_gpi-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if repurchases resumed while Hennessy is being integrated, if a manufacturer invoked a change-of-control clause or refused a franchise transfer, if the proxy statement showed related-party dealings or a board without independent majority, or if the acquired dealerships needed an early impairment. It would improve if disposal proceeds were shown to repay debt, if Conifer's holding stayed clear of the 19% cap, and if post-closing accounts showed the acquired earnings carrying the added interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership percentages, director independence and related-party dealings are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied; this limits the medium governance judgement, which would move to high if leakage to insiders or a conflicted board were disclosed and to low if the proxy showed none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Hennessy dealerships are not in any supplied balance sheet or income statement, so the acquisition-risk finding rests on the company's description and not on acquired earnings, goodwill or cash paid from balance sheet cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Manufacturer mix of new vehicle sales appears only as a chart that did not carry into the text, so the manufacturer dependency finding names Toyota and Lexus as the largest share but cannot size it or show how far Toyota's reduction of dealer support reaches.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 19% cap, the 20% threshold and the buyback link come from the company's own summary of the stockholder agreement and the manufacturer agreements, which were not supplied, so the exact triggers and waiver rights could change how binding the buyback constraint is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The roles behind two executive separation agreements in 2025 are not stated, so no conclusion is drawn on management continuity during the Hennessy integration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The U.K. motor-finance redress outcome is not reported after the annual report, so the finding on U.K. finance and insurance income could be too favourable if redress or broker recourse is imposed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-07-30 Group 1 agreed to buy the assets of 10 automobile dealerships and one collision center in Greater Atlanta, Georgia, with related real estate and leaseholds, and completed the purchase on 2026-10-19 for approximately USD 1.3 billion, subject to post-closing adjustments. USD 80.0 million of the price sits in an indemnity escrow, with 25% released three months after closing, a further 25% after nine months and the remainder after 18 months, subject to pending claims. The purchase is accounted for as a business combination, but the allocation of the price, the goodwill and the pro forma information were incomplete when the report was issued, and manufacturers may impose conditions on the transfer of the 12 franchises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The purchase was financed with the net proceeds of two private placements on 2026-09-22, each of USD 625.0 million issued at par: notes due February 2032 and notes due February 2035, together with cash on hand. The notes are unsecured, guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries, subordinated to senior secured debt and to the liabilities of non-guarantor subsidiaries, and may have to be repurchased on certain asset sales or a change of control; issuance costs were USD 15.9 million and the company expects about USD 80 million of added annual interest expense. A 364-day senior unsecured bridge commitment of up to USD 1.25 billion from JPMorgan, obtained on 2026-07-30, was terminated unused at closing, and the part of the price paid from cash on hand is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In September 2026 the company also signed a master credit agreement with Bank of America for mortgage term loans of up to USD 190.3 million at Term SOFR plus 145 basis points, maturing on 2033-09-23, fully drawn at 2026-09-30 and secured by mortgages on the financed properties, with Group 1 Realty, Inc. as borrower. On 2026-09-21 it signed the stockholder agreement with Conifer, which caps that holder at 19% and, from 2026-11-01, expands the board from 10 to 11 directors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other 2026 activity was smaller: four U.S. dealerships and three U.K. dealerships were bought in the first nine months for USD 219.0 million and USD 0.6 million, one Honda and one Toyota dealership were sold in the third quarter for USD 90.8 million, and seven U.S. dealerships with USD 396.9 million of assets are held for sale, three of them already sold for about USD 235 million after quarter-end. Disposals in the nine months produced a net pre-tax gain of USD 44.2 million in the U.S. and a loss of USD 8.1 million in the U.K.; the date of the three later sales and the use of the proceeds are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier transactions set the base: Inchcape Retail was acquired on 2024-08-01 with 54 dealership locations and three collision centers in the U.K. for approximately USD 517.0 million, USD 500.0 million of notes due January 2030 were issued on 2024-07-30, and the revolving credit facility was extended to 2030-05-30 and enlarged from USD 2.5 billion to USD 3.5 billion on 2025-05-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers below hold the complete record behind the passages above. The sponsor and governance risk level is stated under the sponsor risk assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by shareholder payouts above earnings in 2025 and a debt-funded acquisition in one market, because payouts and acquisition debt reduce the cash and equity buffer ahead of acquired earnings and tie buyback pace to manufacturer approvals, which implies higher sensitivity of leverage and franchise value to a fall in earnings or to an ownership event. Countervailing evidence is the absence of a sponsor, the halt in repurchases after the first quarter of 2026, the Conifer standstill and the retained aftersales profit.

The United States earns 90.93% of group pre-tax income and its income fell 18.67% in nine months and 22.80% in the quarter, so the return of the United Kingdom to a USD 39.6 million profit from a USD 100.3 million loss, which followed 2025 impairments, is the only offset.

The new notes add about USD 80 million of annual interest, so at the last-twelve-months pace of free cash flow the purchase price would take 5.74 years to repay before dividends; the three disposals completed after quarter-end, for about USD 235 million, are the nearer source of deleveraging.

fields.value: The strongest evidence for a firmer view is that reported leverage is lower than derived leverage and parts of the asset base are tangible: the company's covenant ratios were 3.26x leverage against a ceiling of 5.75x and 2.78x fixed charge coverage against a floor of 1.20x at 30 September 2026; net leverage excluding impairments and restructuring was 3.00x, and 4.30x pro forma; 71.26% of dealerships stand on owned property, with mortgage collateral carried at 1.34x the loans at the end of 2025; USD 481.8 million of disposal proceeds arrived in nine months with about USD 235 million more after quarter-end; and U.S. cost removal exceeded USD 50 million a year; after the purchase and the three completed disposals together, net leverage would be about 4.47x. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is the direction of the quarter: gross profit fell 7.06% and U.S. pre-tax income 22.80%, the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 bp on 2026-09-16, and the new notes traded below par within eight days.

It would weaken if gross profit keeps falling at the 2026 pace while selling, general and administrative expenses stay above 71.04% of gross profit, if repurchases resume while pro forma leverage is about 4.73x, if the price was met by drawing the Acquisition Line at its covenant-limited availability, or if the 2032 and 2035 notes trade further below 96.93% and 95.62% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Group 1 sells new and used vehicles, arranges finance and insurance, services vehicles and sells parts through franchised dealerships, with 145 U.S. and 104 U.K. dealerships at 2026-09-30 and 10 more in Greater Atlanta from 2026-10-19. In the first nine months of 2026 revenue was USD 16,188.8 million, of which new vehicles were 48.39%, but new vehicles produced only 19.90% of gross profit; parts and service produced 45.54% and finance and insurance 25.01%. The business model therefore turns a low-margin, cyclical vehicle flow into a steadier annuity of service and finance income, which is what supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, while the vehicle flow, funded by floorplan debt, is what moves with consumer affordability and manufacturer supply.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Group 1 is a listed company with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, which removes sponsor extraction as a risk but also any sponsor backstop. Conifer, one of its largest holders, signed a stockholder agreement on 2026-09-21 that caps its holding at 19%, binds it to vote with the board during a support period and gives it one board seat, scheduled from 2026-11-01, while it holds at least 5%; some manufacturer framework agreements treat ownership above thresholds as low as 20% as a change of control. The notes are issued by the parent and guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries, the U.K. subsidiaries are not stated as guarantors, and the Bank of America mortgage loans are borrowed by a separate real estate subsidiary. The implication is that financial policy rests with management and the board, that buybacks are tied to a ceiling and to manufacturer approvals, and that creditors of non-guarantor subsidiaries, which may include U.K. lenders, rank ahead of the notes on those subsidiaries' assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by unit volumes and by price and mix, and in 2026 volumes are the weak side: in the first nine months retail new units fell 4.8% and retail used units 8.7%, while new vehicle prices rose 2.6% and used prices 4.2%, so revenue fell 4.7% and gross profit fell 5.61%. Management and the filing attribute the fall to affordability pressure, inventory limits on some brands and, in the U.S., a strong comparison period before tariffs; in the U.S. same-store parts and service gross profit was flat while same-store finance and insurance gross profit fell 9.6% on fewer units and lower penetration. Pricing power over new vehicles is limited because competitors buy from the same manufacturers on the same terms, so the earnings that can be defended are aftersales and finance income, and these depend on the number of vehicles sold and serviced and on warranty work billed to manufacturers. The credit implication is that revenue is cyclical and discretionary at the vehicle line and recurring at the service line, which supports a durable cash-flow floor but not growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; calculation C19; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Selling, general and administrative expenses are the largest operating cost below gross profit and absorbed 71.04% of gross profit in nine months of 2026 against 69.82% a year earlier and 67.24% in 2024, so costs have fallen more slowly than gross profit; the U.S. same-store ratio rose to 69.1% from 65.9%. The company cut nearly 700 U.S. full-time positions in April 2026 and says it exceeded a target of USD 50 million of annual savings, and part of pay is commission that falls with gross profit, which gives some cost flexibility, but the quarter still ended at 72.32%. Floorplan interest of USD 66.3 million in nine months was almost fully offset by manufacturer assistance of USD 64.9 million, 97.89% of the cost, and one large manufacturer has said it will reduce such assistance, which would move straight into cost of sales. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure, but not against a combined fall in volumes, assistance and finance income without a further cost programme.

fields.value: Capital spending was USD 244.9 million in the last twelve months, 1.13% of revenue and 26.90% of EBITDA, and USD 167.1 million in nine months against depreciation of USD 93.3 million, 1.79x; the company says spending is driven by acquisitions, new franchises, relocations and manufacturer image programmes, so part of it is discretionary and part is tied to manufacturer requirements, and no maintenance split is given. Working capital moved against the company: payables and accruals absorbed USD 145.3 million in nine months and the company's own adjusted operating cash flow was USD 350.4 million against USD 500.0 million a year earlier. Cash taxes were USD 73.8 million and cash interest USD 220.2 million in nine months. The implication is that EBITDA converted to free cash flow at 24.86% in the last twelve months, so debt reduction depends on disposals and on a recovery of operating cash flow, and the capital spending that can be deferred is a cushion of uncertain size. After the coupon on the new notes, last-twelve-months free cash flow would be about USD 145.8 million before any tax shield, interest saved on repaid revolver borrowings or acquired earnings, and EBITDA cover of cash interest would be about 2.55x.

fields.value: The issuer is the parent, Group 1 Automotive, Inc., and every figure is consolidated. Debt principal at 30 September 2026 was USD 3,913.7 million: four senior unsecured note series totalling USD 2,500.0 million, being the 4.00% notes due 2028-08-15 of USD 750.0 million, the 6.375% notes due 2030-01-15 of USD 500.0 million, the 6.250% notes due 2032-02-01 of USD 625.0 million and the 6.625% notes due 2035-02-01 of USD 625.0 million, issued by the parent with no co-issuer stated; real estate debt of USD 1,112.2 million secured on mortgages, of which USD 190.3 million is the Bank of America term loans at Term SOFR plus 145 basis points due 2033-09-23; finance leases of USD 285.2 million; and other debt of USD 16.4 million. The 6.375%, 6.250% and 6.625% notes are guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and rank behind senior secured debt and the liabilities of non-guarantor subsidiaries; the filings do not describe a guarantee of the 4.00% notes. Unamortized issuance costs of USD 27.6 million take the balance sheet figure to USD 3,886.2 million. By year the maturities are USD 750.0 million in 2028, USD 500.0 million in 2030, USD 625.0 million in 2032, USD 190.3 million in 2033 and USD 625.0 million in 2035; current maturities of USD 261.8 million fall within twelve months, and the amortisation by year of the other USD 1,223.5 million, being real estate debt of USD 921.9 million, finance leases and other debt, is not stated.

fields.value: By facility at 30 September 2026, the U.S. Floorplan Line had USD 1,750.0 million of commitment, USD 1,122.1 million outstanding net of the offset account and USD 627.9 million available, of which USD 153.0 million is immediately available cash in the offset account and the rest can be used only for vehicle inventory. The Acquisition Line had USD 1,750.0 million of commitment, USD 12.3 million of letters of credit, no borrowings and USD 1,442.4 million available. The Ford Motor Credit facility had USD 200.0 million of commitment, USD 161.7 million drawn and USD 38.3 million available, and the General Motors Financial facility had USD 376.7 million, USD 209.1 million drawn and USD 167.6 million available, both usable only for those manufacturers' vehicles. Unrestricted cash was USD 881.5 million. The revolving credit facility matures on 2030-05-30 and no facility is stated to expire within twelve months, but a floorplan borrowing must be repaid on sale of the vehicle and in any case within one year. The two maintenance covenants are a total adjusted leverage ratio below 5.75x, reported at 3.26x against 3.14x at 2025-12-31, and a fixed charge coverage ratio above 1.20x, reported at 2.78x against 3.28x, with no step-down printed; the derived net leverage of 3.30x differs from the reported 3.26x because the company's definitions were not supplied.

Finance leases of USD 285.2 million are inside the debt figure. The filings describe no defined benefit pension plan, only 401(k) and U.K. personal pension matching of USD 18.8 million and USD 12.4 million in 2025, and a search of the five filings finds no factoring, supplier finance, purchase commitment or consent decree. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the third quarter of 2026 the company signed the Conifer stockholder agreement on 2026-09-21, issued USD 625.0 million of 2032 notes and USD 625.0 million of 2035 notes at par on 2026-09-22, drew USD 190.3 million of Bank of America term loans, sold one Honda and one Toyota dealership for USD 90.8 million and agreed to sell seven more, held for sale at USD 396.9 million of assets. After quarter-end it completed the Hennessy purchase on 2026-10-19 for about USD 1.3 billion, with USD 80.0 million held in an indemnity escrow released in three stages over 18 months; the USD 1.25 billion bridge commitment ended unused and the special redemption feature on the 2032 notes lapsed; and three of the seven held-for-sale dealerships were sold for about USD 235 million. A Conifer designee was scheduled to join the board on 2026-11-01. No document dated after 2026-10-29 was supplied, so nothing between that date and the as-of date of 2026-11-18 is established.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high and local: franchised competitors have access to the same vehicles on the same terms and Group 1 has no purchasing cost advantage, so competition falls on location, service and price, and the weak pricing power in new vehicles shows in new vehicle gross profit per unit, which fell 5.6%. Entry by manufacturers selling directly, and the agency model in the U.K. under which the dealer earns a fee and records no vehicle sale, inventory or floorplan interest, threaten the vehicle line and would shrink both revenue and floorplan debt, so the service line would carry more of the profit. Buyers are price-aware and affordability-constrained, which reduces units. Manufacturers hold the strongest position among the forces because they allocate vehicles, set franchise terms and fund floorplan assistance, so supplier power over margins and over the right to operate is high. The credit implication is that margin durability rests on aftersales and not on the vehicle line, and that manufacturer decisions are a likely external trigger for a step change in earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These factors are material because they act on demand, cost of funds and asset values. The Federal Reserve raised its target range by 25 bp to 3.75% to 4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the 2025 annual report puts a 100 bp change in rates at about USD 27.2 million of annual interest expense after swaps, so on that basis the increase alone is worth about USD 6.8 million a year; the designated swaps of USD 653.0 million fix SOFR at 1.21% and mature between December 2026 and December 2031, so the USD 23.6 million of hedge gain due to be released in the next twelve months fades as they expire. Tariff changes, the 2026 emissions rulings and the proposed Euro 7 standard in the U.K. add cost and uncertainty to vehicle availability and affordability, and the Middle East conflict has raised fuel prices and constrained supplies of base oil used in service. The U.K. motor finance redress scheme could reduce U.K. finance income and create broker recourse, and no outcome is reported after the annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are four. The aftersales and finance and insurance profit pool supplied 70.55% of nine-month 2026 gross profit, and U.S. same-store parts and service gross profit was flat while the vehicle lines fell, which steadies debt service through the vehicle cycle. Liquidity before the purchase, at USD 2,477.0 million on the company's definition, and reported covenant ratios of 3.26x against a 5.75x ceiling and 2.78x against a 1.20x floor, give room that the weaker earnings have not yet used. Owned property, at 71.26% of dealerships, and disposal proceeds of USD 481.8 million in nine months give secured borrowing and asset-sale options. Fixed-rate unsecured funding, with USD 1,250.0 million placed in 2026 and no note or revolver maturity before the 2028 notes of USD 750.0 million, gives time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are five. Net leverage is about 4.73x pro forma and only 24.86% of EBITDA reached free cash flow in the last twelve months, so deleveraging is slow. Gross profit is falling faster than costs, with selling, general and administrative expenses at 71.04% of gross profit. Earnings are concentrated, with the United States earning 90.93% of group pre-tax income while its income fell 18.67%. Goodwill and franchise rights equal 94.78% of equity, so the cushion beneath the debt is mostly intangible and would grow with the Hennessy goodwill. Manufacturers control vehicle supply, franchise rights and USD 64.9 million of floorplan assistance, and liquidity after the purchase is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is a strength: last-twelve-months revenue was USD 21,768.7 million across 249 dealerships at 2026-09-30, though market share is not stated. Competitive advantage is average, because competitors buy vehicles on the same terms and franchises are non-exclusive, with the aftersales business the main differentiator. Diversification is average: dealerships span 17 U.S. states and 60 U.K. towns and cities, but 72.20% of revenue is U.S. and the Hennessy purchase adds 12 franchises in one metropolitan market. Cost and capital spending flexibility is average, helped by commission-linked pay and discretionary spending but limited by manufacturer image programmes. Margin stability is average and slipping, with gross margin of 16.0% against 16.2%. Free cash flow stability is weak, at 24.86% of EBITDA in the last twelve months. Ability to refinance is average: the 2026 placement shows access, but quarter-end fair values are below par. Liquidity is strong before the purchase, at USD 2,477.0 million on the company's definition, and not established after it. Financial policy and governance is average: payouts were cut in 2026 after exceeding free cash flow in 2025, and there is no controlling holder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are aftersales profit, liquidity before the purchase, owned property and fixed-rate funding. The main constraints are leverage after the purchase, thin cash conversion and falling gross profit. The trend since 2024 is weaker: EBITDA fell from USD 1,022.2 million in 2024 to USD 855.1 million in 2025 and recovered to USD 910.4 million in the last twelve months, while net leverage rose from 2.82x to 4.29x and then eased to 3.30x before the purchase, and total debt stood at 4.27x EBITDA, up from 4.11x at 30 June 2026, because the new notes pre-funded the purchase. The missing datapoints are acquired earnings, post-closing liquidity, covenant definitions, a rating and peer financials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the company-specific tailwinds are the cost removal in the United States, the swap gains of USD 23.6 million due to be released in the next twelve months, disposal proceeds of about USD 235 million already received and the U.K. return to profit; these support margin resilience and debt reduction. The headwinds are the added interest of about USD 80 million, affordability and rate pressure on units, the Toyota reduction in dealer assistance, integration of Hennessy in a single market and the 2028 notes falling due in about 21 months; these pressure free cash flow, liquidity and refinancing confidence. Over three to five years the sector headwinds are direct selling and agency models, new brands in the U.K., emissions rules and tariffs, and the tailwind is growth in customer-pay repair orders and the company's investment in service capacity; the credit consequence is that the aftersales share of profit decides how much of the vehicle cycle the debt can absorb. The company has given no forecast.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C23; calculation C36; 10-K_2025-12-31_gpi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gpi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a further fall in vehicle demand from affordability pressure, higher rates and tariff-driven prices, with a manufacturer reducing dealer assistance. The first operational break is gross profit: vehicle gross profit and finance income fall with units, as new units fell 3.5% and used units 10.5% in the third quarter, while costs stay sticky, with selling, general and administrative expenses at 72.32% of gross profit in the quarter. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and lower operating cash flow, with payables unwinding as in 2026, and more floorplan interest cost as assistance falls. On pro forma net debt of USD 4,304.7 million, EBITDA at the 2025 level of USD 855.1 million gives 5.03x, and a further 5.61% fall in last-twelve-months gross profit with costs unchanged gives EBITDA of USD 715.9 million and 6.01x. The consequences are tighter covenant availability on the Acquisition Line, little free cash flow to repay the purchase and a 2028 refinancing at higher coupons. Management levers are the unused buyback authorization of USD 306.3 million, the remaining held-for-sale dealerships, deferral of discretionary capital spending of USD 244.9 million a year and further cost cuts. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, since the price is 52.48% of reported liquidity, but both scenarios leave leverage above the pro forma 4.73x. The observable triggers are the quarterly gross profit and cost ratio, floorplan assistance, used units and covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Group 1 presents an adequate business profile supported by aftersales and finance income, scale and owned property, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of about 4.73x pro forma, falling gross profit and thin free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak for the group, due to free cash flow of only 24.86% of EBITDA in the last twelve months, although the service line is steadier than the vehicle line. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on disposals reducing debt, the earnings of the acquired dealerships and the pricing of the 2028 refinancing, with USD 750.0 million due in about 21 months. The primary downside path is a further fall in vehicle gross profit with sticky costs and reduced manufacturer assistance after the purchase has consumed liquidity. Further analysis would require the post-closing balance sheet, acquired earnings, covenant definitions, a rating and peer financials. Top risk: leverage after the Hennessy purchase.
